learning.title: A probe-read-execute runner must run the action's own authorize guard in the probe
learning.trigger: An operation reads the provider outside a transaction by wrapping the authority runner in a probe, a read step and a second authority run (the shape of the ticket operation runner and createResourceUpdateRunner).
learning.mistake: The probe skips the registry's own next, so an action registered with DeveloperAndAdmissionAuthority and a policy.authorize guard was not checked before the provider reads: an unauthorized principal could trigger them. Tests could not tell task:write apart from run:write because no built-in role holds one without the other, and a Viewer lacking a read permission answers 404 on that read while a missing write answers 403.
learning.rule: Call action.policy.authorize in the probe, before the first provider read, and test it with a principal that holds exactly one of the two permissions (a custom role on a guest membership, or a permission_grants row for a viewer) plus a spy that proves zero provider reads on refusal.

verification.requirement: A refused call performs no provider read, and removing the probe guard fails a test.
